pr_title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Remove NULL reference to cfg srv
pr_body:
Does a NULL check on the Config Server before reading its friend field
in send_friend_status.

Fixes #23177.

Signed-off-by: Trond Einar Snekvik <Trond.Einar.Snekvik@nordicsemi.no>

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Access structure member with a possible NULL pointer
issue_context.body:
File: /subsys/bluetooth/mesh/cfg_srv.c
Function: friend_set, send_friend_status

On line 2681 of the code, in function friend_set, **model->user_data** is assigned to **cfg**.
On line 2692 of the code, if **cfg** is NULL, jump to label send_status where send_friend_status is called and **model** is passed as the first argument.
On line 2656 of the code, in function send_friend_status, **model->user_data** is assigned to **cfg**. **model** is the first formal parameter, so the local variable **cfg** is NULL here.
On line 2659 of the code, when calling function net_buf_simple_add_u8, a member is accessed through **cfg->frnd**, but **cfg** is NULL here.

[https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/cfg_srv.c](url)
comments: The bug is actually the unnecessary check in `friend_set()` since the `cfg_srv_init()` function ensures that `model->user_data` is always non-NULL. Setting low priority for this one since it's essentially harmless, but we should still strive to eliminate dead code like this.
@tluio Not sure why you closed it. We should eliminate the dead code.

> @tluio Not sure why you closed it. We should eliminate the dead code.

Sorry, I am not familiar with github, so I am not sure when issues should be closed. Thank you for reopening it. I will be more careful next time.

review_comments: If checking `cfg != NULL` is really necessary (in which case we should make sure it's done everywhere) shouldn't it be an assert instead of a runtime check? How can you even get to this situation considering that `cfg_srv_init()` will fail if there's no context provided, i.e. you shouldn't be able to exercise any of the cfg_srv code in this case.
Hmm, is the issue that `mod_init()` in `access.c` doesn't propagate errors from the per-module init callback upward? I have a feeling we should fail `bt_mesh_init()` if this happens.

The return value from the init function is ignored by access now, so even if we fail init, we'll still be able to receive mesh messages. 

I agree though, this should be handled on init and removed everywhere else. Do we need additional handling in init in your opinion?

If any of the module init callbacks fails it should be an indication that something's not correctly configured or set up, so I'd just propagate the error all the way up to the caller of bt_mesh_init(). Not sure what exactly you mean by additional handling?
Well, there's another option as well: forget about error propagation and make the init callbacks do asserts instead. Not sure which option is more appropriate.

Global failure sounds right to me. The init callbacks have a return code, so there's no reason to add another way to indicate failure, I think. A third option is to disable only the failing model, but this would probably be a spec violation.

So I can make a separate pull request implementing the suggested error propagation, but that would be a functional change. Could this PR be merged as is before 2.3.0 then, to fix the reported issue, then the proper fix with error returns can come after the code freeze is lifted?
What bothers me is that this isn't fixing really anything. All it's doing is hiding an application bug (missing configuration server context).

I have implemented the required changes for init handling in #25365. 
It's a functional change in the model API, so it should probably wait until after the release. 
I'll close this one.
